transcript: Nothing breaks a training video like a narrator who says your company name wrong. The good news? The fix almost always lives in your script.
A voice reads exactly what's written and guesses at the rest. So listen to the whole narration first, and note every word that sounds off.
If the voice reads WHS as a word, add spaces between the letters. For names, write them how they sound, and keep the real spelling on the slide.
Voices read numbers literally, so write them as people say them. Spell out symbols and units, and rephrase any word with two pronunciations.
Short sentences with clear full stops sound natural, not rushed. Keep one shared pronunciation list, so every deck your team makes sounds consistent.
Once your notes sound right, turn the deck into video. On Pro, a.i. directs it, landing each term as the voice says it. Start at powerpoint2vid.com.
